doc: Intake rules for tests/callback_differential.rs. Data, not code: the test interprets it generically and names no OpenProject module. Rules are read from lib/open_project/plugins/acts_as_op_engine.rb at OpenProject 2725194.

roots.doc: Directories (relative to the checkout) a Zeitwerk constant is looked up in, in lookup order. A `*` segment is one directory. Core first, so a module file never shadows a core constant. acts_as_op_engine.rb:42 adds <engine root>/lib to the engine's eager_load_paths; an engine's app/models and app/models/concerns are Rails' defaults.
roots.list_doc: The last six were added from PatchFileNotFound slag: the module an `include_module` / `prepend_module` call names lives in one of these directories (20 calls, none found in the model roots). A Rails engine autoloads every app/* subdirectory (railties-8.1.4.1/lib/rails/engine/configuration.rb:77-78: `paths.add "app", eager_load: true, glob: "{*,*/concerns}"`), so each is a Zeitwerk root, and `app/<dir>/concerns` is one too. Only the directories the slag named are listed, not every app/* directory, so a name stays findable only where the data says it is.
roots.framework_doc: The last four roots were added so the harvest reads, instead of a table, what the framework registers itself. `lib_static` is a Zeitwerk root: config/application.rb:140 (`config.autoload_once_paths << Rails.root.join("lib_static")`). `activerecord-8.1.4.1/lib`, `activemodel-8.1.4.1/lib` and `activesupport-8.1.4.1/lib` are the Rails gems at the version Gemfile.lock pins (activerecord :327, activemodel :325; `activemodel (= 8.1.4.1)` requires activesupport at the same version); their files are named after their constants (active_record/base.rb defines ActiveRecord::Base). `ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base`, so every model's superclass chain ends in `ActiveRecord::Base` and its include-time callbacks (for instance `before_validation :normalize_changed_in_place_attributes`, activemodel-8.1.4.1/lib/active_model/attributes/normalization.rb:14, reached through `ActiveRecord::Attributes`, activerecord-8.1.4.1/lib/active_record/attributes.rb:10) are registered before the model's own. The gem directories exist only where `vendor/bundle` is installed.

roots.indexed_doc: Files loaded by `require`, not by their constant's name, found by the constants they define. The core plugins: config/initializers/00-load_plugins.rb:42-44 puts `lib_static/plugins/<name>/lib` on the load path (`$:.unshift lib`) and each init.rb requires its file (`acts_as_attachable/init.rb:30`); the file acts_as_attachable.rb defines Redmine::Acts::Attachable, not ActsAsAttachable. The gems: Gemfile.lock:360 (acts_as_list 1.2.6) and :463 (closure_tree 9.8.0); acts_as_list/active_record/acts/callback_definer.rb defines ActiveRecord::Acts::List::CallbackDefiner.

engines.doc: An engine is a class whose superclass is one of `superclass`, in a file named `file_name` under any `search` directory. `plugin_module` is the engine constant minus its last segment (acts_as_op_engine.rb:106, `self.class.to_s.deconstantize`).

engine_order.doc: Every patch runs inside `config.to_prepare` (acts_as_op_engine.rb:107, :118, :362). An engine's to_prepare blocks are queued by its `add_to_prepare_blocks` initializer, and engine initializers run in railtie order, which is the order the gems were required. The engine order is therefore the order of the module gems in `file`. Within one engine, calls run in statement order. An engine not listed sorts last, by name.

patch_rules.cite: lib/open_project/plugins/acts_as_op_engine.rb:116-129 (`patch_with_namespace`); the second pattern is the `rescue NameError` fallback (:122-124)

phase.doc: A patch is applied in to_prepare, after the target class body has loaded, so its declarations register after the model's own. `include` runs the module's `included do` block at that moment (ActiveSupport::Concern#append_features, concern.rb:129-140); `prepend` runs only the prepended block (concern.rb:142-152) and registers no callback. A module already in the ancestors is not included again (acts_as_op_engine.rb:111, :368).

macros.doc: Class-level macros whose registrations are read from the macro's own `def`, not listed here. `dsl` is the call in a class body, `file`/`def` the method it runs, `cite` why that call runs that method (the module that defines it is included or extended into ActiveRecord::Base). Each `verify` line is checked against the checkout by the test. ruff reads the `def` (events::macro_ore_from): declarations in order, includes, `send :include`, `class_eval` blocks, hand-overs of the class to another module's method (`Definer.call(caller_class, ...)`) and calls of other methods of the same file. A statement it cannot read (a conditional, a call on another receiver) is listed unread; nothing is evaluated.

defines.cite: closure_tree-9.8.0/lib/closure_tree/support_attributes.rb:43-45 (`hierarchy_class_name` is `"#{model_class}Hierarchy"`); support.rb:61 (`parent_class.const_set(short_hierarchy_class_name, Class.new(abstract_base_class))`) and :63 (`hierarchy_class.class_eval do ... end` registers `belongs_to :ancestor` and `:descendant`); `abstract_base_class` (support.rb:46-58) is the model's first abstract ancestor, which for a model whose superclass is ApplicationRecord is ApplicationRecord (app/models/application_record.rb `self.abstract_class = true`)
